meta.title: Cosmo user guide – Tasks, habits, OKRs and calendar
meta.description: Learn how to use Cosmo: create tasks, track habits with a heatmap, plan your calendar with time-blocking and manage your OKRs. The complete guide.

chrome.heading: User guide
chrome.contact: Got a question? Reach us at

start.title: Getting started
start.subtitle: Create your account and get to know the app in 2 minutes.
start.step1Title: Create an account or try the demo
start.step1: Head to the home page. Click **Get started for free** to create an account with your email, or **Try the demo** to jump straight into a pre-filled version with no sign-up.
start.step2: From the sign-in window, click **Continue with Google** to authenticate in one click with your existing Google account.
start.step3: The left sidebar takes you to the Dashboard, Tasks, Calendar, Habits, OKRs, Statistics and your company space. Collapse it with the **[** key to give your content more room. **Ctrl+K** (**⌘K** on Mac) opens the command palette, and **?** lists every keyboard shortcut.
start.tip: **Demo mode** is ideal for exploring every feature with realistic data before creating your real account. Demo data is not carried over into your account.
start.cardDashboardDesc: An overview of everything you're working on
start.cardInboxDesc: Shared tasks and lists, contact requests, company invitations

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.subtitle: Organize, prioritize and keep track of everything on your plate.
tasks.step1: Click **New task** at the top of the page. Only the name is required; due date, category, priority, duration and lists are all set in the same panel. Even faster: press **N** from any page and type the task as a single sentence.
tasks.step2: Every task gets a priority from **1 (very high)** to **5 (very low)**. Priority 1 shows in red, priority 2 in orange. Sort or filter by priority to focus on what really matters.
tasks.step3: Tick the circle to the left of the task, or on a phone swipe it to the right. It leaves the active view; find it again with the **Done** filter. A recurring task creates its next occurrence the moment you tick it.
tasks.tip: Quick add (**N**) understands the date and four symbols: **#health** for the category, **!!** for the priority (!!! = 1, !! = 2, ! = 3), **~30m** for the duration. The date words are French for now: « Appeler le dentiste jeudi #santé !! ~30m ». Enter creates the task and keeps the field open for the next one.
tasks.featBookmarkDesc: Star an important task: it gets a gold highlight and shows up in the Starred filter.
tasks.featDurationDesc: Set a duration for each task. The Dashboard then shows your total workload.
tasks.featFiltersDesc: Starred, Done, Overdue and Shared combine with each other, as do categories, the priority range and the scope (All, Personal, Company). The / key opens search.
tasks.featBoardDesc: Switch from List to Board: four columns (To do, In progress, Blocked, Done) to drag your tasks between.
tasks.featSubtasksDesc: Break a task that's too big into steps you tick off. A subtask that grows can be turned into a task of its own.
tasks.featDependenciesDesc: Mark a task as waiting on one or more others: it then shows how many tasks are still blocking it.
tasks.featRecurrenceDesc: A task can repeat every day, every week or every month.
tasks.featCollabDesc: Share a task with one of your contacts from the Share tab of its panel. It lands in their inbox, then they can follow and complete it from their own account.
tasks.featCategoriesDesc: Attach each task to a colored category (Work, Personal, Health...) to see where your time goes.

lists.title: Lists
lists.subtitle: Group your tasks by project or context for effortless organization.
lists.step1: At the top of the Tasks page, in the lists bar, click **New list**. Give it a name and a color. The list shows up right away as a new chip next to the others.
lists.step2: In a task's panel, pick one or more lists. The same task can belong to several lists at once, for instance a client and “This week”.
lists.step3: Click a list in the bar to show only the tasks it contains. The counter next to the name shows how many active tasks it holds.
lists.featSmartDesc: Today, Overdue, This week, High priority: their content updates by itself, with nothing to file by hand.
lists.featDefaultDesc: Pin a list so it opens every time you land on the Tasks page.
lists.featShareDesc: Share a whole list with a contact: it arrives in their inbox, with all its tasks.
lists.featColorDesc: Give each list a distinctive color so you can tell them apart at a glance.
lists.tip: Use lists to separate your projects: a **Work** list, a **Personal** list, one per client or per active project. It keeps different contexts from blurring together in a single view.

agenda.title: Calendar
agenda.subtitle: Plan your events and take in your whole week at a glance.
agenda.step1: Click a time slot in the grid, or the **New** button. Set the title, date, start and end time, and category.
agenda.step2: Open the **Tasks** panel and drag a task onto a slot: the event is created with its duration and category, and stays linked to the task. On a phone, tap the task to pick its slot.
agenda.step3: Toggle between **Day**, **Week** and **Month** with the buttons at the top. The Week view strikes the best balance between detail and overview.
agenda.featDragDesc: Drag any event to reschedule it in seconds, without opening a form.
agenda.featRecurringDesc: Create a daily or weekly event once, it repeats on its own. The Recurring button gathers them all.
agenda.featColorsDesc: Each category has its own color. Your calendar becomes a visual dashboard of your time.
agenda.featSlotReviewDesc: Once a task's slot has passed, Cosmo asks whether it got done: you complete it, postpone it or delete it.
agenda.tip: Block time in your calendar for your important tasks (time blocking). It prevents overload and makes your days more predictable.
agenda.note: An event is not a task: the task is the action to tick off, the event is when you do it. Dragging a task into the calendar links the two, and confirming the slot ticks the task.

habits.title: Habits
habits.subtitle: Build routines that last and watch your progress day after day.
habits.step1: Click **New habit**. Give it a name, a duration, a color and, if you like, a category. The habit appears in the tracking board.
habits.step2: Each day, tick the habits you've done by clicking the matching cell in the board: your streak goes up. A habit's menu also lets you schedule it in the calendar or turn it into a task for today.
habits.step3: Toggle between **Table**, **List** and **Global tracking** with the tabs at the top of the page to match the view to what you want to analyze.
habits.streakDesc: The orange counter shows how many days in a row you've done the habit. The streak resets to zero if you miss a day.
habits.rateDesc: Shown in your statistics, it measures the share of days you ticked the habit off over the selected period.
habits.pauseDesc: Vacation, illness: pause a habit, for a set time or indefinitely. Your streak stays intact until you resume.
habits.recapDesc: The Recap button generates an image of your week, ready to share. No task or habit name appears on it.
habits.tip: Start with **2 to 3 habits at most**. It's far easier to build on small regular wins than to burn out on a long list from day one.

okr.title: OKRs: objectives and key results
okr.subtitle: Set ambitious objectives and measure your progress with concrete indicators.
okr.krDesc: A measurable indicator that proves the objective is met. E.g.
okr.step1: Click **New objective**. Give it a title, a category and a deadline (often the end of the quarter). The description is optional.
okr.step2: In the same window, add at least one key result with its target value and unit. Three per objective is good practice. Under **More options**, a weight from 1 to 10 gives a key result more say in the overall progress.
okr.step3: Move a key result forward with the + and − buttons on its card. The objective's progress is computed automatically, weights included. A key result that hits its target is marked **Reached**.
okr.featHealthDesc: Each card shows the share of time elapsed next to your progress: if progress moves faster than the clock, you're ahead.
okr.featCheckinDesc: A quick pass over your key results, one at a time. It also opens by itself at the start of the week from the Dashboard.
okr.featLinkedDesc: From a key result, create a task or schedule an event: they stay attached to it, and the card adds up the time spent.
okr.featCompletedDesc: A validated objective moves to the Completed OKRs list, where you can still view or edit it.
okr.featCategoriesDesc: Sort your OKRs by category (Product, Personal, Team) to keep things organized.
okr.tip: A good key result is **binary or measurable**: either you can put a number on it (e.g. 10,000 users), or it's met or it isn't. Avoid vague wording like "Improve quality".

stats.title: Statistics
stats.subtitle: Analyze your productivity and spot where you can improve.
stats.step1Title: Pick a section and a period
stats.step1: At the top of the page, choose the section to analyze (**Overview**, **Tasks**, **Calendar**, **OKRs**, **Habits**) then the period: **Day**, **Week**, **Month** or **Year**. Every chart updates automatically.
stats.step2: The page opens with a plain-language summary, followed by time invested per period compared with the previous one, then detailed charts for the section. Hover the bars to see the details.
stats.step3: Compare week after week. A steady decline in one area is a signal to adjust your objectives or your habits.
stats.legendTasksDesc: Number of tasks completed per period
stats.legendOkrDesc: Progress gained during the period, objective by objective
stats.legendHabitsDesc: Average completion rate of your active habits
stats.note: Statistics are computed in real time from your own data. The more regularly you use Cosmo, the more the charts reflect how you actually work.

entreprise.title: Company mode
entreprise.subtitle: A full collaboration space: management org chart, teams, projects, team OKRs and fine-grained per-member permissions.
entreprise.step1: In the sidebar, click **Create or join**. Give your organization a name to create it, or enter the company code a colleague sent you to join theirs.
entreprise.step2: Invite one of your contacts directly: the invitation lands in their inbox. You can also share an invite link or the company code; a colleague who enters the code sends a request, which an admin approves.
entreprise.step3: Sections fall into three groups: **My work** (Overview, Tasks), **Steering** (Projects, OKRs, and the Org chart for anyone who manages someone) and **Organization** (Members, Teams, Settings).
entreprise.featPyramidDesc: Every member can have one or more managers. A manager sees the tasks and calendar of their direct and indirect reports, never those of a colleague they don't manage.
entreprise.featRolesDesc: Three roles exist: Admin (runs the organization), Manager (runs a team within the org chart) and Member. The role sets default rights, which can then be fine-tuned one by one.
entreprise.featPermissionsDesc: From the directory, a member's “⋯” menu opens **Edit permissions**: tasks, projects, OKRs, categories, teams, invitations and reports, each right granted or withdrawn individually beyond the role's defaults.
entreprise.featTeamsDesc: Cross-functional teams, independent of the org chart. A team lead manages its members and projects without being a company admin.
entreprise.featProjectsDesc: Create shared projects, assign them to members, and archive them once done. A project's tasks stay visible to the whole team that has access to it.
entreprise.featTasksDesc: Assign a task to one or more members, set dependencies between tasks (one can't start before another is done), and track their progress together.
entreprise.featOkrDesc: Shared objectives, visible to the whole company, to certain teams, or to a chosen list of people. The ones you contribute to also appear on your OKR page.
entreprise.featReportsDesc: In beta, from Overview or Settings: the company report is reserved for admins by default, and a team lead reads their own team's.
entreprise.featInviteDesc: Three ways to bring a member in: invite them from your contacts, share an invite link, or give them the company code (with admin approval). A newcomer arrives unplaced; an admin then places them in the org chart.
entreprise.tip: Place each member in the **org chart** first (who manages whom) before fine-tuning individual permissions: the defaults already follow the role and the position in the org chart, so the exception should stay the exception.
entreprise.note: Company mode is currently free, whatever the size of your team: no tier is billed for the time being.
